exposure: Gestational age (extremely preterm, very preterm, moderate to late preterm)
cohort: 23,803 singleton deliveries at gestational weeks 24+0 - 36+6 between 2004 and 2014
finding: While attempted vaginal breech delivery at extremely preterm and very preterm gestations did not increase the risk of adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes at age four, it was associated with an increased risk of visual impairment and autism spectrum disorders in moderate to late preterm births.
mod_finding: At extremely preterm and very preterm gestations (weeks 24 + 0-31 + 6), no association between a trial of vaginal breech delivery and neurodevelopmental delay occurred; however, at gestational weeks 32 + 0-36 + 6, the risks of visual disability and autism spectrum disorders were increased after an attempted vaginal breech delivery as compared to vaginal cephalic delivery.
